D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official guide describes search tools and booking deeplinks. Agentman reports readOnly annotations on seven tools and an acting `change_flight` tool; Manufact reports zero tools with readOnly/destructive hints. This conflicts on annotation coverage. 2. No server-enforced confirmation step is documented. The guide says booking is completed on the website. 3. OAuth scopes, product-role inheritance, admin switches, client allowlists, token lifetime, and revocation are unknown; provided OAuth metadata requests were blocked. 4. The documented setup uses the global endpoint. Search modes and filters are described; no read-only endpoint or toolset/URL filtering was found. 5. The guide says the MCP Server does not store personal or payment information. No field-level masking or other data boundary is documented. 6. The guide documents result sorting and search filters. Agentman describes a 1–20 max_results range for accommodation searches; no general rate limit or MCP quota was found. 7. Agentman tool descriptions specify date, airport-code, and destination-ID requirements and describe normalizing inverted price ranges; no independent server validation behavior is documented. 8. MCP logging and telemetry behavior: Unknown. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, or reporting tool was found in the reported eight-tool list; no MCP upsell mechanism was documented. 10. Agent-facing directions appear in third-party captured tool descriptions; no official MCP skill delivery mechanism was found. 11. Session state: Agentman says alternative-flight results are stored for later `change_flight` calls; broader memory or cross-session persistence is unknown. 12. The reported tools form one flight/hotel search and selection surface; no sub-server hierarchy was found. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or general request tool appears in the reported list.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official machine-readable tool list or tool names were found on the vendor guide or corporate announcement. The Claude connector directory names one tool (`search_flights`); ToolJunction also lists one. Agentman and MCP.so report eight tools, and Manufact reports eight tools from its endpoint scan. The actions list uses Agentman's captured tool names and descriptions; all eight are labelled third-party because the names are absent from vendor sources. Catalogues differ: Claude and ToolJunction show one; Agentman, MCP.so, and Manufact show eight.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: A person can complete the booking on lastminute.com after opening the returned deeplink. The MCP guide says final booking occurs on the website and that booking issues or changes to existing reservations should go to customer support; no reservation lookup, payment, booking-change, or cancellation tool is documented in the official guide.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The official guide offers example prompts and describes default, filter, and ranking search modes. Agentman tool descriptions give additional agent-facing steps, including silently resolving a destination before hotel search and preserving returned price text. These are documented directions; no public code was available to establish server enforcement.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The official guide states: “The MCP Server does not store personal or payment information”. It says final booking occurs on lastminute.com. No retention period, AI training policy, MCP audit log, or scope model was found in the reviewed documentation.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The guide describes real-time travel data, price comparisons, flexible search filters, recommendations, and direct booking deeplinks. It states that final booking takes place on lastminute.com.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The available evidence supports website handoff for final booking and a search/selection-oriented tool surface. The no-storage statement is a vendor documentation claim; the reviewed public evidence does not expose server implementation to verify it. Third-party scans disagree on tool annotation completeness.

contradictions: The official configuration guide describes flights, hotel-only stays, and flight-plus-hotel packages but does not name tools. The Claude connector directory and ToolJunction list only `search_flights`, whereas Agentman, MCP.so, and Manufact report eight tools, including hotel and package searches.

lastminute.com's January 2026 announcement calls the flight server its first MCP step and describes hotel and dynamic-packaging systems as roadmap work. The later technology guide (version 2, last updated February 2026) describes hotel and package searches at the same endpoint.

Agentman reports readOnly annotations on seven tools and an acting `change_flight` tool; Manufact reports zero tools with readOnly/destructive hints and flags state-changing tools without destructive hints. The third-party observations differ on annotation coverage and classification.
observations_for_research: The documented flight search presents price-sorted, server-filtered, and recommendation-ranking modes, with distinct behavior described for each.
The guide directs the user to complete booking on the vendor website through deeplinks; the reported tool set includes a package-flight change before booking but no reservation-management action.
Agentman reports cross-call session state for alternative flight options used by a later flight-selection action.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, every prepared official page's text/HTML/script extract, and the local code folder. No official source repository or package was found. The vendor guide and corporate announcement name no MCP tools. Tool names and schemas therefore come from third-party directory material; Agentman says its listing reflects an endpoint scan, and Manufact reports an eight-tool scan. The supplied OAuth responses were used as received; Cloudflare blocked metadata reads. An unofficial lastminute-deals activity-booking server appeared in links.json and was excluded as an unrelated name collision. Pricing and the corporate privacy-policy page contained no MCP-specific fee or detailed MCP data-handling terms in the prepared extracts.
